nodes.label: dv-bar-001
nodes.text: Title: descriptive, reflects the main insight.

nodes.label: dv-bar-002
nodes.text: Always use axis titles unless the labels are obvious (both axes).

nodes.label: dv-bar-003
nodes.text: X-axis: categories (+ optional tick marks) with per-category labels; Y-axis: values with incremental labels. Grid lines aid scale comprehension.

nodes.label: dv-bar-004
nodes.text: Key: required when using alphanumeric labelling.

nodes.label: dv-bar-005
nodes.text: Filtering/config tools (optional): above the chart.

nodes.label: dv-bar-006
nodes.text: Grouped extras: optional separator line between groups; group category label (description); group key for alphanumeric group labels.

nodes.label: dv-bar-007
nodes.text: Positive + negative values: vertical bars only. Don't put negative values on a horizontal bar chart. Scope: positive-scale bar charts. Negative values use the vertical below-zero form, which is the sanctioned way to show them. (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: dv-bar-008
nodes.text: Projected states: always label past vs projected.

nodes.label: dv-bar-009
nodes.text: All bar charts must include a zero baseline for the Y-axis.

nodes.label: dv-bar-010
nodes.text: Arrangement: values/categories well spaced, evenly distributed. Don't use too many categories — split into multiple charts or switch chart type.

nodes.label: dv-line-001
nodes.text: Zero y-axis is OPTIONAL here — use it only when it aids interpretation. ⚠ Deliberate asymmetry with bar charts, where the zero baseline is mandatory. Record both; never let a bar rule bleed into line enforcement.

nodes.label: dv-line-002
nodes.text: Different-shaped markers per data set (not colour alone — pairs with the parent "don't rely on colour" rule). Single data set: markers not required.

nodes.label: dv-line-003
nodes.text: Axis titles unless obvious; per-category X labels, incremental Y labels; grid lines for scale.

nodes.label: dv-line-004
nodes.text: Reference point + tooltip: tooltip repeats the data point's values on both axes without obscuring the chart.

nodes.label: dv-line-005
nodes.text: Measurement intervals comparable, similar scale; single-axis grid for large intervals, double-axis for small; drop gridlines if they confuse.

nodes.label: dv-line-006
nodes.text: Dual y-axes only for different measurement units, clearly labelled — key states which axis each set refers to.

nodes.label: dv-line-007
nodes.text: Multi-set charts: include filter/focus functionality; consider show/hide toggles for lines and markers.

nodes.label: dv-line-008
nodes.text: End-line markers + key when markers would obscure small intervals; colours distinguish sets. Projected states: clear labelling; trends: end-line markers.

nodes.label: dv-line-009
nodes.text: Aspect ratio: match the height of the surrounding content — never exaggerate the spark's proportions.

nodes.label: dv-line-010
nodes.text: In tables: group all data related to the spark sequentially — never split it.

nodes.label: dv-line-011
nodes.text: Straight lines between data points. Never gratuitous curves for aesthetics — they distort the data.

nodes.label: dv-pie-001
nodes.text: Start at 12 o'clock; order slices largest → smallest (unless categories have an inherent order — then plot that order, consistently across the journey).

nodes.label: dv-pie-002
nodes.text: Label + exact proportional value per slice; indicator lines to connect value/label with closely-spaced segments; key when labels are alphanumeric.

nodes.label: dv-pie-003
nodes.text: Doughnut centre: total value + descriptor together — never a descriptor without the value.

nodes.label: dv-pie-004
nodes.text: Direct labelling adjacent to segments (from the parent guideline).

nodes.label: dv-pie-005
nodes.text: Labels/values inside a slice only when there's space to stay readable.

nodes.label: dv-pie-006
nodes.text: Slice-ordering direction (clockwise/anti-): check assistive-technology accessibility.

nodes.label: dv-pie-007
nodes.text: Never enlarge or pull out slices to emphasise scale in user journeys.

nodes.label: dv-pie-008
nodes.text: ## Usage Proportion of a set total only. Not for comparing one group to another — a pie shows group size relative to the whole.

nodes.label: dv-pie-009
nodes.text: Maximum 6 slices — both pie and doughnut. More than 6 categories → combine the smallest into a single "Other" slice, or use a different chart type.

nodes.label: dv-pie-010
nodes.text: Values must add up to the total sum; always include value indicators.

nodes.label: dv-pie-011
nodes.text: Always indicate when values are rounded.

nodes.label: gai-003
nodes.destinyFull: TASTE at source, but this is precisely what the gate stack mechanises
nodes.text: Quality assurance — "outputs must meet HSBC's high visual standards — avoid using any content that appears synthetic or does not reflect our premium brand values".

nodes.label: gai-004
nodes.text: Contextual appropriateness — real imagery for real-world topics (news, locations); gen-AI permitted for visionary concepts ("Smart Cities 2050") and for localising backgrounds/clothing in real photographs; never to add or alter people.

nodes.label: gai-005
nodes.text: No AI-generated people in marketing/storytelling; no cloning of real HSBC personnel; critical exceptions escalate to the Living Wall.

nodes.label: gai-006
nodes.text: Motion avatars — internal, functional content only (e.g. training), clearly marked AI-generated; never marketing, never replicating real personnel.

nodes.label: gai-007
nodes.text: Ethical standards — data privacy, bias, accountability for outcomes (Responsible AI page, staff-only). Plus, from the permitted/prohibited table: never edit, add or remove religious or political items.

nodes.label: gai-008
nodes.text: The tool is in-scope, twice. Apollo is (a) itself a generative-AI tool needing lifecycle approval at any HSBC-like client, and (b) a producer of brand-foundation outputs (data-vis, typography, colour) whose outputs sit under Living Wall governance. Adoption planning must include both.

nodes.label: hex26-002
nodes.text: Two REFRESH DELTAS with asset impact: (a) the Iconic Hexagon is now used at a smaller size than previously; (b) the Cropped Hexagon is reduced to one-edge and two-edge crops — three- and four-edge crops are RETIRED. ⚠ Any 2025-era hexagon assets/masks in the repo need a vintage check before reuse (`hexagon-masks.md` is legacy-era).

nodes.label: hex26-005
nodes.text: Graphic treatments (3D Hexagon, Graphic Hexagons, Keyline Hexagon…): guidance "will be released soon." ⚠ Source gap, same class as the grey palette (col26-001) — recheck cadence.

nodes.label: icon-001
nodes.text: Icons and pictograms are not interchangeable; don't scale icons up in place of pictograms.

nodes.label: icon-002
nodes.text: Don't use illustrations as icons (site echoes our icon-source rule at brand level).

nodes.label: icon-003
nodes.text: Don't substitute product/3rd-party logos with icons; utility app icons are a separate branding application (App tile guidelines).

nodes.label: icon-004
nodes.text: Avoid icons without labels unless universally recognisable ('home', 'save', 'search') — and verify the universal meaning with user testing.

nodes.label: icon-005
nodes.text: Functional icons need a minimum 44×44px target area.

nodes.label: icon-006
nodes.text: Minimum 16px, maximum 48px; scale proportionately in 2px increments. The floor is legibility; the ceiling is the icon/illustration boundary — at the ceiling an icon is close to illustration dimensions; and the fixed set holds consistency. (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: icon-007
nodes.text: Rationalise a standardised size set (e.g. 18/24/36/48) per toolkit/journey; don't use uneven scales.

nodes.label: icon-008
nodes.text: Match icon size to the accompanying text size; don't pair dramatically differing sizes (see Links guidelines).

nodes.label: icon-009
nodes.text: Thicker-weight variants (1.8px on the same grid — Figma layer) exist for use below 16px, e.g. combined with text; chevrons + some status icons. Only thicker chevrons alongside text links.

nodes.label: icon-010
nodes.text: When icons indicate a function, use the active version to differentiate default vs selected; colour may support the distinction.

nodes.label: icon-011
nodes.text: Icons require 4.5:1 contrast in all instances — "like text", labelled or not.

nodes.label: icon-012
nodes.text: Code: icon with label → `alt=""` (null); icon without label → `alt` = icon name.

nodes.label: icon-013
nodes.text: RAG-coloured notification/status icons: maintain contrast against actual background; never colour alone for status — supporting information required.

nodes.label: icon-014
nodes.text: "Do not export SVGs from the HSBC Icon Library file or artwork files. Download the SVGs from the UI Centre for sharing with development." Our Figma-exported catalogue (`assets/icons/`) is for internal knowledge-base prototyping only; dev handoff sources from the UI Centre.

nodes.label: icon-015
nodes.text: Icon contrast: 4.5:1 vs our 3:1. The hub states icons need 4.5:1 "in all instances" because they're interactive and legibility-critical; pictograms 3:1 (+ descriptive alt). This RESOLVES the `col26-007` REVIEW item (brand page "text and icons 4.5:1" vs supporting page "graphics 3:1"): differentiated by asset class — icons 4.5 · pictograms 3 · chart/RAG indicators 3. Gate impact: our text/icon cont

nodes.label: icon-016
nodes.text: Size floor tension. Site: minimum 16px (thicker-weight set below that). Toolkit tokens: `xsmall = 12px`. Consistent only if xsmall implies the thicker-weight set — toolkit doesn't say. 📌 RULED (Dave, desk pickup): the full 12–48 range is permitted for now — "prune if we have to". Toolkit export stays operative; no gate encoding.

nodes.label: icon-017
nodes.text: Max-size tension. Hub: "three sizes 18/24/36, never scaled larger." Standard page: max 48, example set includes 48. Deeper page wins provisionally (48), but the source disagrees with itself. 📌 RULED (Dave, desk pickup): 12–48 permitted, same ruling as icon-016.

nodes.label: ill-001
nodes.text: Never use illustration as the principal creative medium — photography first.

nodes.label: ill-002
nodes.text: Limit the number of colours within an illustration; use HSBC Red tactically to draw focus.

nodes.label: ill-003
nodes.text: Build illustrations from geometric shapes — squares, circles, triangles.

nodes.label: ill-004
nodes.text: Don't mix mediums — no illustration composited with photography.

nodes.label: ill-005
nodes.text: Don't use 3D rendered objects.

nodes.label: ill-006
nodes.text: Don't use caricatures; don't make illustrations cartoonish; no keyline styles; no over-complex characters or fine detail; abstract only if understandable at a glance; present wide cultural diversity, tailored per market.

nodes.label: ill-007
nodes.text: Never use data visualisation or RAG palettes for illustrations. ⚠ SUPERSEDED 2026: the unified supporting palette explicitly grants "the full supporting palette" to illustration (see `colour-standards-2026.md`). Under the refresh this rule inverts from "separate palettes" to "one palette, shared". Old rule kept for pre-refresh work only.

nodes.label: ill-008
nodes.text: Stick to a single level of illustration through a customer experience.

nodes.label: ill-009
nodes.text: Don't use object illustrations as icons or pictograms — those have their own visual style.

nodes.label: ill-010
nodes.text: Don't use typography within illustrations.

nodes.label: logo26-001
nodes.text: An HSBC logo appears at least once on every piece of communication or customer journey. In a native app the journey's logon or splash screen satisfies the rule — "the user summoned an HSBC app, they know where the destination is". (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: logo26-008
nodes.text: The masthead logo is the FULL-COLOUR Masterbrand on BOTH grounds, in ALL FOUR THEMES — `masterbrand-light-colour` on light, `masterbrand-dark-colour` on dark, in Apollo Legacy, Apollo Mono, Apollo Console and Apollo Supercharge alike. A monochrome theme does not make a monochrome masthead: mono is not the masthead lockup in any theme. `va25-015` says a Masterbrand appears in ALL digital mastheads; this names WHICH VARIANT. Dave answered "Full colour both grounds — masterbrand-light-colour on light, masterbrand-dark-colour on dark" on all four theme rows of his own export. (s282-D5, Dave 2026-09-18)

nodes.label: logo26-009
nodes.text: Digital clear space is a FLOOR, not the print rule: vertical clear space ≥ 0.25 × logo height, snapped UP to the 4px grid. At the five `s282-D3` steps that is 24 → 8 · 28 → 8 · 32 → 8 · 36 → 12 · 40 → 12 px. It is a floor, not a value: anything at or above it that itself sits on the 4px grid is legal. Dave's words: "The logo dimension based clear space is really for print, we have a rule of thumb for digital is half of this dimension, but it isn't a rule, maybe we have it set as a floor of 0.25 snap-up to the 4px grid, so at 24 height we have 8px as the floor fer the vertical clearspace, as long as it snaps to 4px above that I'm comfortable". ⚠ HIS NOTE SAYS VERTICAL. HORIZONTAL clear space is NOT STATED AND IS NOT RULED — it is carried open (W-282ll), never completed by symmetry. The logo-dimension clear space (`va25-014`, 1× hexagon height on all sides, `visual-assets.md`) remains the PRINT rule and is untouched. (s282-D5, Dave 2026-09-18)

nodes.label: logo26-010
nodes.text: The hexagon alone may be used on the nav-rail head, the app tile and the favicon — each conditional on Create Direct approval AND "HSBC" in view (`va25-016`'s two conditions stand, unrelaxed) — and in responsive layouts at the smaller sizes, tablet-portrait and mobile, where the Masterbrand does not fit. Dave's words: "The pure logomark can also be used in responsive layouts when we get to smaller sizes, tablet-portrait and mobile". This answers `s230-D2`'s declared residue — "App-shell-nav-rail deliberately NOT rebound (56px rail head, no lockup fits)": a lockup now fits, and it is the hexagon. (s282-D5, Dave 2026-09-18)

nodes.label: mot-001
nodes.text: Move along 45° and 90° angles.

nodes.label: mot-002
nodes.text: Use masks, not fades; straight cuts for scene transitions; never fade or crossfade. Transitioning without a hexagon = straight cut.

nodes.label: mot-003
nodes.text: "Move with confidence — motion should be deliberate and not playful or bouncy."

nodes.label: mot-004
nodes.text: Motion complements and enhances; never distracts.

nodes.label: mot-005
nodes.text: Any motion over 5 seconds needs play and pause.

nodes.label: mot-006
nodes.text: Don't overuse motion principles in a timeline; deploy at key points, let content shine.

nodes.label: mot-007
nodes.text: "Not playful or bouncy" vs our promoted spring physics. Button "Refined scale-physics" (canon, 2026-06-22) uses an overshoot spring (`motion/easing/spring` ≈ cubic-bezier(.5,1.7,.4,1)); Selection-controls exploration is "deliberately springy". The brand standard says deliberate-not-bouncy across all platforms including apps. Read available: our scale-only, small-amplitude physics IS "confident and

nodes.label: nam-001
nodes.text: Never possessive with product names — "HSBC should not appear in the possessive form": never "HSBC's Credit Card" / "HSBC's Easy Invest"; write "An HSBC Credit Card" / "HSBC Easy Invest".

nodes.label: nam-002
nodes.text: Names are never fully capitalised — "CONNECTED MONEY" banned; capitalised first letters + lowercase ("Connected Money"). Action-suggesting multi-word names may close up (PayMe, InvestDirect).

nodes.label: nam-003
nodes.text: Lock-ups are maintained in text for business propositions — always "HSBC Premier", "HSBC Advance"; the HSBC prefix protocol is HSBC + functional descriptor, with judgment to reduce repetition of "HSBC" in running text.

nodes.label: nam-004
nodes.text: Labels over invented names for standard services — "Live Chat" is a recognised label and needs no name ("Chat To Us" adds complexity). First question is always "is a name required?".

nodes.label: nam-006
nodes.text: No new icon, logo or brand identity for a name — names follow the current brand identity guidelines.

nodes.label: neuro-001
nodes.text: Simple pages; only elements relevant to the current task. Design-review-level rule; success depends on the rest of the section.

nodes.label: neuro-002
nodes.text: Page-length caps (at 1280×1024): index pages ≤4 vertical view lengths (non-mobile), article pages ≤5.

nodes.label: neuro-003
nodes.text: Separate sections clearly: ≥20px whitespace between sections; separators/control boundaries ≥3:1 contrast (best practice 4.5:1).

nodes.label: neuro-004
nodes.destinyFull: ADVISORY-derivable in part (above-fold purpose = heading present in first viewport)
nodes.text: Important information top, above the fold; page purpose determinable without scrolling (1280×1024); front-load information. Equal-importance items: alphabetical or chronological.

nodes.label: neuro-005
nodes.text: Every page carries a short purpose summary — in the heading structure, banner, or first paragraph.

nodes.label: neuro-006
nodes.text: Banner/hero caps: initial images/banners ≤30% of page height; carousels and videos ≤30% (at 1280×1024).

nodes.label: neuro-008
nodes.text: Symmetry + layout stability: max 2 different column layouts per page; no significant mid-page layout changes; grid on homepages, single column on content pages.

nodes.label: neuro-010
nodes.text: Links and buttons visibly clickable: underline links; visited links change colour (best practice); button boundaries ≥3:1. ⚠ The :visited leg is a REAL canon gap — no snippet or canon.css styles :visited at all (checked 2026-07-02). 📌 RULED (Dave, 2026-07-02 eve): neuro best practice adopted as direction — visited links should differ in colour; implement at the next Links touch (supercharge candid

nodes.label: neuro-014
nodes.text: Avoid lots of bright colours: soft, harmonious combinations; bright colours ≤20% of screen content. Autistic users prefer low-contrast schemes — note this is about AREA of saturation, not permission to break contrast floors (floors still apply).

nodes.label: neuro-016
nodes.text: Minimum font size 12pt (exceptions: sub/superscript, T&Cs, related). ⚠ pt-vs-px: 12pt = 16px CSS at the standard 96dpi reading — under which our S6 (14px) and S7 (12px) standard-text sizes would fail; under a loose "12pt≈12px" reading our scale complies (S7=12px floor, 12px reserved for legal = mirrors the exception). The web type scale page and the store both treat 14px/12px as legitimate.

nodes.label: neuro-019
nodes.text: Line height ≥1.5× font size; paragraph spacing ≥2× font size. WCAG 1.4.12 receipt. Our scale: S5 16/24 = 1.5 exactly ✓; S6 14/20 ≈ 1.43 ✗; S7 12/16 ≈ 1.33 ✗ — same family of tension as neuro-016/webf-031; the brand's own scale sits below the neuro floor for small sizes.

nodes.label: neuro-020
nodes.text: ≤4 sentences per paragraph; ≤240 characters per sentence (incl. spaces).

nodes.label: neuro-021
nodes.text: Don't interrupt text flow with images; callout quotes only at section ends; no scroll-stoppers.

nodes.label: neuro-022
nodes.text: Bold for phrases only — never whole sections/lists; emphasis not structure.

nodes.label: neuro-023
nodes.text: Clear, concise language at the audience's reading age (WCAG 3.1.5 receipt; does not impact regulatory requirements).

nodes.label: neuro-024
nodes.text: Avoid metaphors and ambiguity. The standard EXPLICITLY flags the tension: tone of voice supports "conversational, informal" style, but literal readers need unambiguous writing. ✅ RECONCILED 2026-07-02 by the tone-of-voice ingest — the brand's own standard partitions the licence: expressive is SURFACE-scoped (headlines, good news, marketing), literalness is FUNCTION-scoped (actions, instructions, w

nodes.label: neuro-025
nodes.text: Avoid jargon/abbreviations/acronyms/idioms; define acronyms on the page (WCAG 3.1.3/3.1.4 kin; Style Guide has further guidance).

nodes.label: neuro-026
nodes.text: Icons/visuals support text, never replace it — content must remain comprehensible with all images and icons removed. Carve-out by reference: unpaired icons are allowed only for the universal set named in `icons.md` ({#icon-004}); pictograms stay no-exception ({#pict-001}). (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: neuro-028
nodes.destinyFull: TASTE + the sole-carrier leg is neuro-026
nodes.text: Simple images, understood within ~2 seconds; single object in focus. Image content never the sole carrier of information.

nodes.label: neuro-029
nodes.text: Meaningful images only — congruent with the page story, adding value/clarity.

nodes.label: neuro-030
nodes.text: Background images sparingly; no content/form inputs overlaid on decorative images; uniform-texture backgrounds acceptable; non-patterned backgrounds on content pages.

nodes.label: neuro-034
nodes.text: Text intro above every video (what it's about + implied length).

nodes.label: neuro-036
nodes.text: Attention-attracting movement is a LAST resort — use size/colour/font emphasis first. BUT: "small, animated movement of an arrow when moused over communicated that the section was clickable... limited and explainable, users did not find it disturbing" — an empirical receipt that small, purposeful HOVER motion aids comprehension.

nodes.label: neuro-041
nodes.text: Small-type neuro-compliance cluster. neuro-016 (12pt minimum, strict reading = 16px) + neuro-019 (≥1.5 line-height; S6/S7 sit at 1.43/1.33) both indict the brand's OWN type scale for small sizes if read strictly. Since the type scale page and the toolkit export agree on S6/S7, loose readings are almost certainly intended (12pt≈12px; 1.5× aspirational for body = S5 ✓). 📌 RULED (Dave, 2026-07-02 eve

nodes.label: neuro-042
nodes.text: Calm-by-default vs expressive register. neuro-006 (hero ≤30% height), neuro-014 (bright colours ≤20% of screen), neuro-001/-028 (simplicity) collectively define a measurable "calm ceiling". The expressive register (charter §4, dual-live palettes) pushes the other way. These are not contradictions — they're the two dials of the fixed/flex charter with NUMBERS on the sober side for the first time. G

nodes.label: neuro-044
nodes.text: Communication guidance is a hub we did not descend — 7 scenario subpages (meetings, multimedia, media, digital content, internal comms, surveys, social media). Scenario 4 (digital content) is the engine-relevant one.

nodes.label: photo26-001
nodes.text: Style: cinematic, immersive, human, authentic — frame stories; human perspective required, people optional; muted, sophisticated tones (never too vibrant); red appears tactically and NATURALLY (warmth in lens/scene, not forced accents); lead with photography as the principal creative medium.

nodes.label: photo26-002
nodes.text: HARD bans: no Generative AI, mixed media or CGI-rendered elements in imagery; no montages/composites; no staged/posed/clichéd shots; no text as a mask. ⚠ The gen-AI ban is PIPELINE-CRITICAL: a generation engine must never fabricate photographic imagery — photography comes from the Global Image Library/approved sources only. Direct kin of the gen-AI governance regime (gai-*); Apollo's imagery story = retrieval from licensed libraries, full stop. The gen-AI clause carries a review date — review by 2027-03 — which changes nothing about the ban until then. (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: photo26-003
nodes.text: Shot vocabulary: cinematic · people (real moments; diversity; disability shown positively; natural warmth in skin tones) · landscapes/cityscapes (lived-in viewpoints, not landmark clichés) · objects (lower-funnel, curated, product-linked) · textural (macro) · abstract (mood, photography-based).

nodes.label: pict-001
nodes.text: Every pictogram carries a label or copy that underpins its meaning — no exceptions (unlike icons' universal-meaning carve-out). The usage boundary: a pictogram supports a concept; an icon signals an action. (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: pict-002
nodes.text: Not a replacement for icons or illustrations; never interchange.

nodes.label: pict-003
nodes.text: Don't use pictograms as a replacement for a hero illustration.

nodes.label: pict-004
nodes.text: Use levels to reflect message importance; don't mix levels in components representing messages of equal prominence.

nodes.label: pict-005
nodes.text: Keep metaphors simple and globally recognisable; avoid unnecessary abstraction (bowl + steam, not the bowl's contents). Abstract designs only for figurative concepts (FX, sustainability) and never reliant on prior knowledge.

nodes.label: pict-006
nodes.text: No designs without a clear relationship to the message they support.

nodes.label: pict-007
nodes.text: Don't place pictograms on a red background — interferes with the red accent and causes contrast issues with the primary form.

nodes.label: pict-008
nodes.text: ≥3:1 contrast against the background in all placements, with clearly descriptive alt text. L1 on dark backgrounds only with white lines; L1 over photography only where the background doesn't compromise contrast; nothing on visually busy imagery.

nodes.label: pict-009
nodes.text: No drop shadows — elevation is functional-only (an object moving over another), which a pictogram never needs.

nodes.label: pict-010
nodes.text: Digital: minimum 60px, maximum 192px, proportional scaling at 2px intervals. Below 60px, use an icon instead. The figures are consistency and enforcement against misuse by designers, not a perceptual threshold. (s282-D1, Dave 2026-09-17)

nodes.label: pict-011
nodes.text: Never squash, stretch, skew or distort; scale with locked aspect ratio.

nodes.label: pict-012
nodes.text: Don't position different-scale pictograms immediately next to one another in common components; max 3 distinct sizes per experience, logically chosen.

nodes.label: pict-013
nodes.text: Non-digital (print, physical): scale proportionally to the format with sufficient clear space; legibility at small sizes.

nodes.label: pict-014
nodes.text: Pictograms are a component-library gap. The engine's 38 components include icons (sprite + gate) but no pictogram asset class at all — no tokens, no assets, no manifest entry. If generated experiences ever include pictogram-bearing patterns (empty states, onboarding, confirmation illustrations), this class needs onboarding: distinct contrast rule (3:1 + alt), distinct size floor (60px), level syst

nodes.label: tov-001
nodes.text: The HSBC voice = four principles: Human, Insightful, Confident, Intelligent wit. Together they are the brand's verbal identity — "customers should be able to recognise us by how we write and speak" the same way they spot the palette and logo.

nodes.label: tov-002
nodes.text: The voice does not change by channel; the mechanics do. "Our voice doesn't change, regardless of whether we're writing a letter, email, text or tweet" — channel rules (below) tune length and structure, never identity.

nodes.label: tov-004
nodes.text: Say 'we' and 'you'. First person plural for the bank, second person for the reader. "We're writing to you about your current account", never "Today HSBC is communicating to all current account customers".

nodes.label: tov-005
nodes.text: Use contractions — single contractions only. I'm, we'll, you're, can't, won't, don't. Never double contractions ('wouldn't've', 'shouldn't've'). Writing words out in full is allowed for deliberate emphasis ("I will").

nodes.label: tov-006
nodes.text: Formal→human word substitutions (merged principles-page + FAQ tables, 17 pairs): advise/inform→tell · assist→help · cease→stop · commence→start · continue→carry on · converse→talk · endeavour→try · enquire/request→ask · ensure→make sure · funds→money · obtain/receive→get · provide→give · require→need · therefore→so.

nodes.label: tov-007
nodes.destinyFull: TASTE at generation + tov-008/009 make it measurable
nodes.text: Plain English, no financial or legal jargon; familiar words wherever possible. Readability is framed as an inclusion measure (age, education, ESL, text-reader users, ADD/autism/dyslexia/dyspraxia).

nodes.label: tov-008
nodes.text: Readability floor: Flesch-Kincaid 70+ / grade ≤7 (reading age 11) as the general bar for all writing. Source calibration: Harry Potter ≈ the bar; Time magazine ≈ grade 12.

nodes.label: tov-009
nodes.text: Readability targets by artefact type (Flesch Reading Ease): internal email 60–70+ · customer email 60–70+ · customer letter 60+ · social 70+ · report 50+ · technical report 45+ · T&Cs 40+.

nodes.label: tov-010
nodes.text: Active voice, not passive. "We'll send you a closing statement", not "a closing statement will be sent". Passive hides the actor and cools the tone.

nodes.label: tov-011
nodes.text: Main point first. Only what the reader needs to know. What you think the key point is and what the reader needs aren't always the same — decide what matters to *them* before writing.

nodes.label: tov-012
nodes.text: Summary subheadings that carry the key message — skimmable by design; explicitly motivated by a11y (screen-reader navigation, dyslexia/autism) as well as time-poor readers. Headings should summarise ("Tougher markets, tighter margins"), not label ("Outlook").

nodes.label: tov-013
nodes.text: If something is changing, always say why — especially unwelcome news; reasons in ≤2 sentences, no regulation or internal-process detail.

nodes.label: tov-014
nodes.text: No hedging: banned commitment-hedge phrases — 'we're committed to', 'we endeavour to', 'we aim to', 'The Board is committed to'. Say what we're doing: "We're asking you for this information to protect you…". Hedges "make us appear unreliable and non-committal".

nodes.label: tov-015
nodes.text: Always say what happens next — even when it's 'nothing'. Every message that shares information ends with what to expect; "even if no more action is needed, be sure to say that clearly."

nodes.label: tov-017
nodes.text: Specific beats generic: use references that resonate with the named audience (UHNW legacy framing vs student 'pop into a branch'). No two audiences the same.

nodes.label: tov-018
nodes.text: No clichés or stock expressions ("24 hours a day, 7 days a week" = "a cliché any bank could use"). Fresh perspective instead.

nodes.label: tov-019
nodes.text: Colloquialisms show local expertise — BUT functional messages stay literal. Source, verbatim: "neurodiverse readers may interpret language very literally. So stick to clear, unambiguous phrases in functional messages, or when telling readers to take an action." Reconciles neuro-024 — see Findings F2.

nodes.label: tov-021
nodes.text: Don't define the audience too narrowly — readers have overlapping identities (race, nationality, orientation, gender identity, parenthood, neurodiversity, disability, ESL).

nodes.label: tov-022
nodes.text: Gender-neutral defaults: no gendered titles when unknown (use 'Hello [Name]'); -person job titles (chairperson, businessperson, police officer); gender-neutral social roles ('parents/caregivers', not 'mothers'); they/them until told otherwise.

nodes.label: tov-023
nodes.text: Coded-language ban list: blacklist/whitelist → blocklist/allowlist · master-/slave- → primary/secondary · 'long time no see' → 'it's been a while' · 'ethnic' as qualifier → name the actual group/market · 'illegal immigrants' → 'undocumented person'.

nodes.label: tov-024
nodes.text: No umbrella terms (BAME, BME, catch-all 'Asian'); name communities properly; capitalise Black as ethnic/cultural adjective (AP style).

nodes.label: tov-025
nodes.text: Vary example names and cultural references in placeholders, pre-populated fields, and scenario copy across cultures, backgrounds, faiths. ENGINE-CRITICAL: this is a rule about *generated fixture data* — our snippet/gallery placeholder names are in scope.

nodes.label: tov-026
nodes.text: People-first language: person with a disability · has epilepsy, never 'is an epileptic' · never 'suffers from' · 'a reader over 65', never 'elderly'. Identity- first accepted where communities choose it (autistic, Deaf); person-first when unsure.

nodes.label: tov-027
nodes.text: Unwelcome news: MORE human, not more formal. Formality under stress is named as a misconception that "harms the customer experience". Readability stays at grade ≤7; don't dress bad news as good news or force a positive.

nodes.label: tov-028
nodes.text: Sorry once, early, plainly — and only for things we control. "We're sorry for the mistake." Banned insincere apologies: 'we apologise for any inconvenience caused' · 'please accept our sincerest apologies' · 'regretfully, mistakes were made'. No apology for regulatory/market changes.

nodes.label: tov-029
nodes.text: No throat-clearing openers: 'It has come to our attention…' · 'Following a recent review…' · 'As you'll be aware…'. Main point early; for very bad news a one-line preparatory frame is allowed ("We're writing to let you know that…") — and the main message may sit in the heading/subject itself.

nodes.label: tov-030
nodes.text: Unwelcome news ends with options + a warm route in: when the change hits, what impact, what to do with questions, alternatives (switchable accounts, nearby branches), prominent placement, never an abrupt ending.

nodes.label: tov-031
nodes.text: Sensitive subjects: no euphemisms. 'Has died', not 'passed away'; the person's name, not 'the deceased'/'your late husband'. Plain and warm, not sentimental ("insincere coming from a bank"); euphemisms are also a literalness barrier (neuro-024 receipt).

nodes.label: tov-032
nodes.text: Internal comms: same standards + Smart Brevity numbers — updates <300 words, paragraphs 1–2 sentences, open with "What's new" / "Why it matters", sentences <25 words, subheading every 3–4 paragraphs.

nodes.label: tov-033
nodes.text: Good news: no self-congratulation. Banned: 'you'll be delighted to know' + subjective adjectives 'amazing', 'fantastic', 'brilliant' ("salesy and presumptuous"). Let the benefit speak.

nodes.label: tov-034
nodes.text: Calls to action: one message per communication; open AND close with the CTA; signpost with action headings ('What to do now'); consequences stated as fact, not threat; specific deep links, not homepages; numbers + hours in body text, never small print; avoid asterisks/small print generally.

nodes.label: tov-035
nodes.text: Hard-sell ban list: 'simply' (as in 'simply visit') · 'Did you know…?' · 'remember'/'don't forget' · 'Hurry!' · 'Free!' · 'Dear Valued Customer'.

nodes.label: tov-036
nodes.text: Process guidance: soften imperatives ('You'll need to…'), warm form-field labels ('Your details', not 'Account holder's details'; 'Please tell us', not 'Please indicate'), steps in the customer's question-order, say where they are in the process. ENGINE-CRITICAL: form-label warmth + progress-location are component rules (Input-fields, Progress trackers).

nodes.label: tov-037
nodes.text: Forms & attachments: first person; active; ≤2 enclosures; label variable parts (page/section refs); summary paragraph atop long documents; pre-populate what we know; boxes not lines; return-checklist; benefit-framed instructions.

nodes.label: tov-038
nodes.text: Device-agnostic language: 'select', never 'click'; never describe UI visually. Writing must work on desktop, mobile, tablet. Canon swept 2026-07-02: 0 signals.

nodes.label: tov-039
nodes.text: Email: subject carries the why in <8 words; spam-trigger words avoided ('Free', 'Email', 'Buy', 'Cash', '100%', 'Income'); two-scroll length cap; CTA at open and close.

nodes.label: tov-043
nodes.text: Web/PDF: sentences <15 words; ≤3 sentences per paragraph; F-pattern layout awareness (key content top-left, never bottom-right); more subheadings than print; subheadings summarise the paragraph below. ENGINE-CRITICAL: these are the copy numbers for every generated screen.

nodes.label: tov-044
nodes.text: Greetings/sign-offs matrix by line of business: Retail letter 'Dear [first name]'/'Yours sincerely' · Retail email 'Hello'/'Thanks' · Retail text 'Hi [first name]'/'Thanks or thank you' · PB + CMB/GBM letter 'Dear [preferred name]'/'Yours sincerely' · PB + CMB/GBM email 'Hello'/'Thank you' · PB + CMB/GBM text 'Dear [preferred name]'/'Thank you'. Team sign-offs ('Your HSBC Advance Team') unless a n

nodes.label: tov-045
nodes.text: The voice sits mid-scale on formality — never slang, never old-fashioned — so it can adapt per market. Named calibrations: Australia = most informal · France/ Argentina = more traditional (vous/vos) · India/Malaysia = "a few degrees towards formal" (social hierarchy). Clarity always outranks the local adjustment.

nodes.label: tov-046
nodes.text: No idioms where non-native speakers may miss them: 'get started', not 'get the ball rolling'. Local spelling/terminology honoured (cheque/check; Secure Key/ Security Device HK).

nodes.label: type25-003
nodes.text: Never red typography for headlines or body copy — red only for text links (CTAs) and "specific digital toolkit use-cases".

nodes.label: type25-005
nodes.text: Readability numbers: body line length 60–80 Latin characters (avg); headline length 20–50 characters (avg); no orphans (single word alone on the last line of a heading/ paragraph); no widows (word/short group starting a new column or page).

nodes.label: type25-007
nodes.text: No italics — not licensed, and harder to read, especially for people with dyslexia.

nodes.label: type25-008
nodes.text: Emphasis = Univers Bold only, keywords/phrases not sections. No underline for emphasis (underline = links only — neuro-007 dual-source) · no shapes/graphic devices · no drop shadows on text · no outlines or graphic styling on type.

nodes.label: type25-009
nodes.text: Type colour: dark-on-light, light-on-dark; no highlighted type blocks; no long-form copy on red or coloured backgrounds; consider size/scale for headline type on coloured backgrounds.

nodes.label: type25-012
nodes.text: Headlines get breathing space — keep body copy apart from creative headline typography.

nodes.label: type25-015
nodes.text: Hierarchy: lead with a short, instantly understandable headline + concise body; sub-headings distinct from both; CTA sits away from body with more weight, without competing with the headline.

nodes.label: type25-020
nodes.text: Three cost-0 gate candidates surfaced: no-italics scan (type25-007), no-text-shadow scan (type25-008), red-text-role check (type25-003) — all passed canon with zero occurrences. RULED by Dave 2026-07-03: STRAIGHT TO BLOCKING (his override of the advisory-first convention — zero occurrences + exact checks = the advisory step buys nothing). ENACTED as snippet-gate check 6 (`_validate_snippets.py`),

nodes.label: type26-002
nodes.text: Only use brand-approved fonts, weights and colours.

nodes.label: type26-003
nodes.text: All text legible and ≥4.5:1 contrast.

nodes.label: type26-004
nodes.text: Never use red typography except within specific digital toolkit use-cases. Sharpens the col26 red-text rule: the exception scope is toolkit-defined (e.g. CTA links), not designer judgment.

nodes.label: type26-005
nodes.text: "We don't use uppercase or italics lettering — use sentence case." ⚑ This makes the house sentence-case rule (and the G5 all-caps advisory check) source-backed at brand level — and extends it: *italics are also out*. Informs the open all-caps scope ruling on Dave's desk: the source is brand-wide, favouring canon-wide over brief-scoped.

nodes.label: type26-006
nodes.text: Only use lighter font weights for creative headline treatments; favour lighter weights generally, bolder weights only for occasional emphasis (a word, a subheading).

nodes.label: type26-007
nodes.text: Expressive headlines — emphasis, pace, personality without losing clarity; fewer words; never obscure or break a word into illegibility.

nodes.label: type26-008
nodes.text: Balanced bilingual — Latin/Chinese/Arabic given comparable prominence, unified not "translated"; balance layout, hierarchy, spacing, line length.

nodes.label: type26-009
nodes.text: Clear type hierarchy — scale/weight/spacing/placement signal reading order; limit weight levels to the minimum; max two main fonts with a bold option.

nodes.label: type26-010
nodes.text: Headlines: lightest weights (Ultra Light, Thin, Light) at larger sizes; heavier only for a clear hierarchy shift or single emphasis point. Never bold an entire headline — one or two words at most. Body: light/regular. "If everything's bold, nothing is."

nodes.label: type26-011
nodes.text: Hierarchy depth: 3–4 levels (L1 headline, L2, supporting, body).

nodes.label: type26-012
nodes.text: Latin: 12pt minimum, print AND digital. Captions/small legal copy may go to 6pt minimum. Ultra Light/Thin forbidden at small sizes (line too thin to be legible). Chinese (MYing Hei): 14pt body minimum. Arabic: 12pt (as Latin).

nodes.label: type26-013
nodes.text: Black/dark-grey on light · white/light-grey on dark · NO other colours for typography, ever. White-only on HSBC Red and supporting reds; no long-form copy on red or coloured backgrounds; no highlighted type blocks; over photography black or white only.

nodes.label: type26-014
nodes.text: Headline-on-photography contrast: 3:1 large AA · 4.5:1 small AA · 7:1 AAA.

nodes.label: type26-015
nodes.text: "Don't overlay text on gradient backgrounds" (+ digital: verify at viewpoints, no unreadable wrap). ⚠ Collides with charter §4's expressive gradient unlock for surfaces/heroes — heroes normally carry headlines. 📌 PARKED 2026-07-02 (Dave) → ruled at the component-finessing pass, alongside mot-007 ("too expressive" family). Interim discipline: no gradient-hero generation; gradient surfaces are treat

nodes.label: type26-016
nodes.text: Latin headlines: −15 to −30 tracking; leading = size +3pt (50pt → 53pt). Latin body: −5 to −10 tracking; leading "1.1×" — ⚠ but the page's own example is 12pt → 16pt (1.33×), and Chinese body says 1.1× with example 14pt → 18pt (1.29×). Stated ratio and worked examples disagree — likely "1.1×" should read differently or the examples embed channel-specific values.

nodes.label: type26-017
nodes.text: Chinese headlines: leading 1.25×; body 0 to +10 tracking. Fine-tune Chinese punctuation spacing; refine baselines when mixing scripts.

nodes.label: type26-018
nodes.text: No wide kerning that breaks legibility; not too tight either.

nodes.label: type26-019
nodes.text: Title case AND sentence case are the brand-legal casings; uppercase banned outside acronyms (explicitly: harder to read, reduces word shapes, dyslexia/low-vision cost). Note: the house rule (sentence case ONLY, no title case) is *stricter* than brand — house wins locally, no conflict. ✅ ENACTED 2026-07-02 (Dave ruling): canon-wide sweep done — 14 snippets + gallery chrome de-capped (caps tracking

nodes.label: type26-020
nodes.text: Left-aligned is primary; centred sparingly (short headings/labels/callouts, small word counts); right rare ("Headline A of the magnetic type construct"); body copy stays horizontal. Never justified (rivers); avoid hyphenation — rebalance lines instead.

nodes.label: type26-021
nodes.text: Size ratio 1.0× Latin : 0.85× Chinese (perceived-height parity); Chinese one weight step thicker than Latin (Univers Ultra Light ↔ MYingHei Thin · Thin ↔ Light · Light ↔ Regular · Regular ↔ Medium).

nodes.label: type26-024
nodes.text: Balanced dual language — Latin + Chinese + Arabic get comparable prominence, "unified, rather than 'translated' or secondary"; balance layout/hierarchy/spacing/ line length.

nodes.label: type26-025
nodes.text: Give imagery room to breathe: type frames the focal point, sits in clean negative space or along natural composition lines; grids + rule of thirds; clear visual path — headline first, then the image's key detail. Centre alignment is now legitimate in named cases: ambient photography without a focal point (Iconic Hexagon central, with or without text), magnetic headlines centred. ⚠ DELTA vs 2025's

nodes.label: type26-026
nodes.text: Over-photography watch-outs: legibility first — avoid busy areas, high-contrast edges, faces; safe placement, sufficient contrast, "(where needed) a subtle gradient/ overlay, rather than heavy effects"; respect the subject — never cover focal points/ faces/brand cues. ⚠ DELTA vs 2025's flat "no treatments — adjust the asset" (type25-013): the refresh PERMITS subtle overlays as a contrast aid. Inte

nodes.label: type26-029
nodes.text: Magnetic headline (NEW construct): an Iconic Hexagon sits at the CENTRE of the headline line as visual anchor/pivot; words "magnetised" around it; vertical alignment to the hexagon's 5 vertices, baselines to hexagon geometry; photography stays the hero (magnetic block moves to give the subject space; stacked/side variants; centred over ambient scenes); rule of thirds guides, not strict. This is th

nodes.label: va25-001
nodes.text: Inclusion test before any asset: what's the intent? does it help understanding? does it distract, obscure or slow the user? No contextually-irrelevant images "for the sake of layout or design" — "sometimes less is more".

nodes.label: va25-002
nodes.text: Attribute taxonomy — every asset is functional (icons, avatars, logos), informational (product photos, infographics, diagrams, charts) or complementary (photography, illustration) — defined by content nature, not media type. The placement rules below key off this.

nodes.label: va25-003
nodes.text: Visual-engagement tiers set the imagery budget per page type: HIGH (home, hub, landing, promotion) = complementary allowed throughout · MEDIUM (product, service, article) = complementary minimal — header or start-of-section only; informational/ functional carry the weight · LOW (applications, processes) = ONLY assets fundamental to the task; complementary at most at the very start or completion. E

nodes.label: va25-004
nodes.text: Onboarding: new-to-HSBC users may get more complementary assets (if they enhance, never distract); existing customers get focused informational/functional for new features.

nodes.label: va25-005
nodes.text: Pattern consistency across the journey: same asset type for the same pattern everywhere (an illustration on one confirmation page = illustrations on ALL confirmation-class pages); logged-on and logged-off experiences consistent. Named surfaces where this is critical: applications · onboarding · coach marks · tutorials · alerts messaging · status codes (eg 404) · empty states. ENGINE-CRITICAL → con

nodes.label: va25-006
nodes.text: Hierarchy: assets supporting the primary goal outrank secondary-goal assets; avoid conflicts of attention (order, scale, space, contrast, balance).

nodes.label: va25-007
nodes.text: Re-use rules: an asset re-appears only in the same context/metaphor/purpose. Never the same thumbnail linking to different content; never the same hero for different articles/products; never an icon outside its functional context (source example: a memo icon representing fraud content). ENGINE-CRITICAL: the icon SEMANTIC-fit layer on top of the icon-source gate — provenance says which icons exist,

nodes.label: va25-009
nodes.text: Responsive behaviour: test assets across devices; photography adapts by ratio crops; illustrations may need reformatting AND line-weight adjustment per layout/ size. Brand-source receipt for the dynamic-weight concept — the brand itself says line weight is context-dependent.

nodes.label: va25-010
nodes.text: Light/dark modes: assets may need per-mode exports; icons black-in-light get value-reversed in dark (can be code-level). Receipt for the icon-contrast-delta work and mode-aware asset handling.

nodes.label: va25-011
nodes.text: Quality bar: sharp, high-quality, tested on low- and high-DPI — or NO asset at all ("better not to use any visual assets" than bad ones).

nodes.label: va25-012
nodes.text: Placement taxonomy: hero · display · spot · thumbnail · interface, with attribute legality per placement (hero = complementary/informational · interface = NEVER complementary · thumbnail = any) + the placements-by-type matrix (verbatim in `_sources`: video/animation top out at spot; photography/illustration reach thumbnail; avatars/icons/logos live spot→interface; favicons interface-only).

nodes.label: va25-013
nodes.text: Aspect ratios: video/animation 16:9 standard (21:9, 4:3, 1:1 alternates); photography/illustration/infographics 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 (reversible for portrait); icons/avatars 1:1 square — "icons and avatars that appear rounded are likely to have masked the square asset using code"; third-party logos 16:9/4:3. The rounding-is-a-code-mask line is the official mechanics behind the Badge+Avatar round e

nodes.label: va25-014
nodes.text: The page's numeric rules (absent from the 2026 distillation): clear space = 1× hexagon height on all sides; minimum size = 7mm hexagon height / 105×20px / 26×7mm; positioning = top-left or bottom-left, inset 1× hexagon from edges (exceptions: video open/end frames, eye-line adjustment out-of-home).

nodes.label: va25-015
nodes.text: Masthead contract: the Masterbrand logo appears in ALL digital mastheads; clicking it always returns to the root of the CURRENT business line — never cross-line, orientation over surprise. ENGINE-CRITICAL → the Header/masthead component (deferred but queued) inherits this behaviour contract.

nodes.label: va25-016
nodes.text: Never-rules: no new lock-ups from text for departments/programmes/products; never distort, recolour, reorient or recreate; hexagon-only use needs Create Direct approval AND 'HSBC' context nearby (app tile, profile avatar, favicon); never the legacy Times New Roman logo; third-party use follows the TMLA process; Brand Promise lock-up never wraps lines.

nodes.label: va25-017
nodes.text: Variant selection on photographic backgrounds: primary (red hexagon/white infill/black type) on light; white-wordmark version on dark-where-red-reads; mono black on light print, mono-reversed white on dark or HSBC-red; white infill never on mono versions. Expands logo26's dark = full-colour-negative rule with the legibility ladder.

nodes.label: va25-018
nodes.text: No Generative AI, mixed media or CGI-rendered elements in imagery — ALSO the 2025 rule. photo26-002 is therefore vintage-STABLE, not a refresh novelty: the ban has held across both standards. Second receipt for the pipeline-critical rule (engine generates experiences, never photographic assets; library retrieval only).

nodes.label: va25-019
nodes.text: D&I imagery rules: diverse representation across markets; no stereotypes or clichés; represent LGBTQ+ people; portray people with disabilities living their lives — never make the perceived difference the focus; localisation sensitivity per market. Imagery-side kin of tov-025's fixture diversity.

nodes.label: va25-020
nodes.text: Creative considerations (explicitly optional): natural hints of red; hexagon- geometry angles, never a forced 45°; wide 'opening up' frames + intimate close crops.

nodes.label: va25-022
nodes.text: Photography textures always use the red/white/grey palette.

nodes.label: webf-003
nodes.text: Limit colour, especially HSBC red, in dark mode — replace some light-mode colour with white/grey; red kept strategic (primary CTA, hexagon). Every use of red evaluated.

nodes.label: webf-006
nodes.text: Light-bleed compensation. Strong light-on-dark makes type/icon strokes look heavier; counteract with light grey, lowered white opacity, or lighter background — but contrast must still pass accessibility.

nodes.label: webf-010
nodes.text: Dark mode needs more negative space — dark backgrounds make the same layout feel more closed-in.

nodes.label: webf-011
nodes.text: Level taxonomy: 0 = base content (body, imagery, cards, buttons — NEVER elevated) · 1 = sticky content (top navigation, drawer, tooltip) · 2 = modality (partial modals, dialogs) · 3 = notifications (snackbars). Elements contained within a level do not display further elevation.

nodes.label: webf-012
nodes.text: Shadow = specified depth (higher level → deeper shadow); overlay = large, unspecified depth, used to focus. Never display both on the same element/pattern.

nodes.label: webf-013
nodes.text: No purely aesthetic shadows (inner or outer) — elevation is functional.

nodes.label: webf-014
nodes.text: No elevation on patterns that move within level-0 content (e.g. an accordion pushing content down).

nodes.label: webf-017
nodes.text: The responsive-forms URL redirects to an "Elements and patterns (web and app)" stub: element/pattern standards (buttons, accordions, app tiles…) now live in the Common Toolkit; "the Design Toolkit remains the single source of truth" for interaction states, accessibility requirements, usage rules, specifications. ⚠ Source gap: forms standards are not reachable as a page; the Common Toolkit is an as

nodes.label: webf-018
nodes.text: Base unit 4px for horizontal and vertical measurement — "normally express this unit in multiples of 8, however multiples of 4 can be used as a fallback".

nodes.label: webf-025
nodes.text: Hierarchy: Light/Regular/Medium weights build hierarchy; titles/section headers/ subtitles use S1–S4 (≥19px), applied as H1–H4 where semantically correct; page titles use light + regular; 16px recommended body on public-facing sites; 12px reserved for T&Cs / disclaimers / legal; medium weight for highlighting words/phrases, not long paragraphs.

nodes.label: webf-026
nodes.text: Line length 60–80 characters; never full page width on wide layouts.

nodes.label: webf-027
nodes.text: All spacing in multiples of 4, mapping to grid margins/gutters; padding/margins follow the system (e.g. 16px gutters → 16px card side-padding).

nodes.label: webf-029
nodes.text: Pre-refresh vintage. The dark-mode page is dated 2021 and the family reads pre-refresh. Its "limit red / replace colour with white-grey" conservatism sits oddly against the 2026 refresh's expressive direction (dual-live palettes, charter §4) — the living-standard caveat applies: deltas ≠ defects; reconcile when the web pages re-issue under the refresh.

nodes.label: webf-030
nodes.text: "No purely aesthetic shadows" vs `elevation/decorative`. webf-013 bans decoration- only shadows; our store carries `elevation/decorative` (blur 8) alongside `elevation/functional` (blur 16) — from the Figma export. Likely the toolkit means "decorative" as a lighter functional tier, not aesthetic-only, but the name collides with the standard's language.

nodes.label: webf-031
nodes.text: Body leading contradiction, cross-standard. This page: S5 body = 16/24 = 1.5 leading (and our store matches). typography-standards-2026 (type26-016): Latin body leading "1.1×" with worked examples at 1.29–1.33×. Three sources, three ratios — strengthens the type26-016 suspicion that "1.1×" is a misprint or channel-specific. The web scale + our store agree at 1.5 for web body; operative.

nodes.label: webf-032
nodes.text: `gap/fixed/content/xxsmall = 2px` breaks the 4px base unit. The standard says multiples of 8, fallback 4; the toolkit export carries a 2px gap. Toolkit-wins stance (grey ramp, icon sizes) says keep it operative, but it's a real toolkit-vs-standard contradiction.

nodes.label: webf-033
nodes.text: font-1..4 sizes are TScale-mode-dependent — check the export carries them. `typography.json` has fixed sizes only for font-5..7 (correct — S5–S7 are invariant); font-1..4 sizes/leading must vary by scale mode. If the semantic-scale export didn't carry per-mode type values, large-type generation at scale-2/3 is running on a gap.

nodes.label: webf-034
nodes.text: Responsive spacing values (R units) are a source gap. `spacing.json` is fixed-only; the RScale VALUES per breakpoint aren't in the store or on this page (likely toolkit- internal). Generation currently has no responsive-spacing dimension.
